title: Supported Defence: Hold Munich
briefing: Industrial era. You are Germany with one walled city, Munich (size 5). A Rifleman holds it, and three more of your Riflemen stand next to it on the east side. Three Indian Riflemen stand next to it on the west side, and India is at War with you. This tries a new rule, supported defence: order a unit into your own city while the enemy attacks it and it supports the city from where it stands. The walls take the first damage. What gets through is shared between the garrison and every supporter, and each of them strikes back at the attackers. If the garrison falls, the supporter that can take the most damage moves in. The city falls only when the garrison and all its supporters are dead. A supporter the enemy attacks where it stands gives no support that turn. Hold Munich for 8 turns. Does supporting a city feel right, and can three attackers still take it?

lab.question: Does supporting a city feel right, and can three attackers still take it?
lab.blurb: Munich is walled and held by one Rifleman. Three Indian Riflemen stand at its west gate; three of yours stand just east of it.
lab.opponent: India follows a fixed plan: every unit it has marches on Munich and attacks once three stand near it, and it never makes peace.
